title: Industrial surplus exchange

stages.name: interpretOffers
stages.algorithm: Translate surplus descriptions into functional properties, quantities, condition, and known limitations. Distinguish verified specifications from seller assumptions, preserve ownership and handling restrictions, and identify information needed before proposing a consequential reuse.
stages.gate: No unsupported material property or transferable-title claim.

stages.name: interpretNeeds
stages.algorithm: Recover the actual purpose behind recipient requests, separating essential performance from preferred form. Identify acceptable adaptations and nonnegotiable constraints, including evidence or specialist approval needed for unfamiliar materials or equipment.
stages.gate: Recipient confirms constraints that determine suitability or safety.

stages.name: generateReuse
stages.algorithm: Propose conventional and inventive matches based on function rather than product names. Explain the adaptation mechanism and uncertainty, include multi-item bundles when useful, and reject creativity that depends on relaxing essential requirements or unapproved handling.
stages.gate: Essential fit is evidenced; speculative compatibility creates a qualification task, not an allocation.

stages.name: assembleExchange
stages.algorithm: Construct feasible multi-party exchanges using exact quantity, reservation, and transport services. Account for dependent legs, storage windows, and adaptation costs, and preserve unallocated surplus and unmet needs explicitly.
stages.gate: No double allocation, unsupported capacity, or negative quantity.

stages.name: verifyTransfer
stages.algorithm: Coordinate approved transfers and verify quantity, condition, ownership, and recipient acceptance at handoff. Record rejected or partially accepted material and update future matching evidence without falsely reporting a completed reuse benefit.
stages.gate: Transfer and acceptance evidence support reported quantities and outcomes.

operational_details: A material is offered by weight but needed by volume: require density evidence before exact conversion.
An offer is withdrawn after matching: invalidate dependent exchange legs before confirming them.
Equipment has unknown maintenance history: require qualification rather than assuming operability.
A recipient accepts only part of a lot: release remaining quantity back to availability.
A creative reuse requires specialist approval: keep the match provisional until that approval exists.
